messages.author: df02280efc34f7be
messages.subject: Another get.real() question - density predictions
parts:
Hi all, I'm updating some old code and trying to obtain predictions of density using get.real(). This is a multi-session model with camera trap grids stratified by urbanization level (categorical). My top model includes an effect of urbanization category on density: D ~ Urb_class, p0 ~ b + Urb_class, sig ~ sex + Urb_class

When I try to obtain density estimates for each Urb_class using the following new data frame, I'm getting an error message:

nd.D <- data.frame(Urb_class = factor(c("Urban", "Suburban", "Exurban")))

predict.D <- get.real(model = top.model,
                                  type = "dens",
                                  d.factor = 400,
                                  newdata = nd.D) 

Error in eval(g., envir) : object 'd.beta.Urb_classUrban' not found 

In this thread (https://groups.google.com/g/oscr_package/c/YZvGlGnIwjs/m/hwtt-l_dAgAJ) Ursa was getting a similar error, evidently because the factor variable was being incorrectly interpreted as numeric. However, this doesn't seem to be the case with my model, since the output shows Urb_class as a factor:

Model:  D ~ Urb_class p0 ~ b + Urb_class sig ~ sex + Urb_class
 Run time:  41.23795  minutes
 AIC:  7498.326
 
Summary table:
                         Estimate    SE       z P(>|z|)
p0.(Intercept)             -2.319 0.240  -9.681   0.000
t.beta.Urb_classSuburban    2.685 0.466   5.765   0.000
t.beta.Urb_classUrban       0.781 0.313   2.494   0.013
p.behav                     3.771 0.263  14.347   0.000
sig.(Intercept)             4.607 0.084  55.153   0.000
sig.sexmale                 0.492 0.051   9.577   0.000
sig.Urb_classSuburban      -1.115 0.098 -11.331   0.000
sig.Urb_classUrban         -0.798 0.098  -8.185   0.000
d0.(Intercept)              0.168 0.088   1.913   0.056
d.beta.Urb_classSuburban   -0.591 0.122  -4.838   0.000
d.beta.Urb_classExurban    -2.294 0.193 -11.903   0.000
psi.constant               -0.562 0.154  -3.636   0.000
*Density intercept is log(individuals per pixel)
  Nhat(state-space) = exp(d0.)*nrow(ssDF)
  (caution is warranted when model contains density covariates)

Any thoughts on what I might be doing wrong? Thanks in advance for your help and for all the useful advice in this Google Group!

Cheers,
Claire


P.S. In case it's relevant, I have no problem making predictions for p0 or sigma when I construct the data frames below. This thread (https://groups.google.com/g/oscr_package/c/YZvGlGnIwjs/m/hwtt-l_dAgAJ) was very helpful for the sex-specific sigma predictions. 

nd.p0  <- data.frame(Urb_class = rep(c("Urban", "Suburban", "Exurban"), each = 2),
                  b = c(0,1))

nd.sig <- data.frame(Urb_class = rep(c("Urban", "Suburban", "Exurban"), each = 2),
                  sex = rep(factor(c(0,1)), 3))

messages.author: df02280efc34f7be
messages.subject: Re: Another get.real() question - density predictions
parts:
Well, after messing with this all day I might have answered my own question half an hour after posting :) For whatever reason, it seems like get.real() won't predict density when the reference level for a categorical variable ("Urban", in my case) is named in the new data frame. This works: 

nd.D <- data.frame(Urb_class = c("(Intercept)", "Suburban", "Exurban"))

As mentioned, this only seems to be an issue when predicting density, not p0 or sig (which I think is part of why I was so confused!)
